name: Self-Directed Queries Complexity / Recursive Teaching Dimension
details: For nonempty finite binary concept classes on finite domains, $\mathrm{SDC}(\mathcal H)\ge\mathrm{RTD}(\mathcal H)$.
proof: The survey theorem applies the mistake-transcript teaching argument to every nonempty subclass and uses the recursive-elimination characterization. It proves $\mathrm{RTD}(\mathcal H)\le M_{\mathrm{sd}}(\mathcal H,X)$ and the stronger projected bound $\max_{S\subseteq X}\mathrm{RTD}(\mathcal H_{|S})\le M_{\mathrm{sd}}(\mathcal H)$.
witness_verification: For any fixed $d\ge3$, Ben-David--Eiron's Lemma 1 gives $\mathrm{SDC}(\mathcal C_n^d)\ge n$ while $\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal C_n^d)=d$. Hu--Wu--Li--Wang's explicit quadratic VC-to-RTD bound gives $\mathrm{RTD}(\mathcal C_n^d)\le39.3752d^2-3.6330d$, independently of $n$. Thus $\mathrm{SDC}/\mathrm{RTD}$ is unbounded along this family.
proof_source: CombinatorialParameters/main.tex, Theorem thm:selfdirected-teaching; recursive characterization le:tpd. Doliwa--Fan--Simon--Zilles Lemma 7 and Corollary 8(1) give the classical whole-domain comparisons.
